import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 64

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/64](https://www.erdosproblems.com/64)
-/

namespace Erdos64

/--
Does every finite graph with minimum degree at least $3$
contain a cycle of length $2^k$ for some $k \geq 2$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_64 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V) [Fintype V] [DecidableRel G.Adj],
        G.minDegree ≥ 3 → ∃ (k : ℕ) (v : V) (c : G.Walk v v),
            k ≥ 2 ∧ c.IsCycle ∧ c.length = 2^k := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): add more context

end Erdos64

review.notes: The sole declaration, Erdos64.erdos_64, faithfully states the source’s question. Its quantifiers, minimum-degree threshold, cycle predicate, exponent bound, and answer scope agree. The live cited page returned a Cloudflare challenge, so its full statement and remarks were read through the July 9, 2026 archive; current independent status sources also record the problem as open. The stronger large-degree result mentioned in the source does not settle minimum degree three. Scratch checks compiled successfully: complete graphs on 0–6 vertices have minimum degrees [0,0,1,2,3,4,5]; minimum degree at least three forces at least four vertices; and an explicit four-cycle in K₄ satisfies the conclusion. Also proved that, for nonempty finite graphs, the minimum-degree hypothesis is equivalent to every vertex having degree at least three. All experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
